title: Consumer Groups
subtitle: Coordinated horizontal scaling of consumers with dynamic partition assignment and cooperative rebalancing.
keyTakeaways: A Consumer Group allows a fleet of worker instances to scale consumption horizontally: each partition in a topic is consumed by at most one worker in the group.
If a topic has 8 partitions and a consumer group has 10 instances, 2 instances will sit completely idle with zero assigned partitions.
The Cooperative Sticky Assignor eliminates catastrophic stop-the-world rebalance storms by revoking and reassigning only the specific migrating partitions.

  [ Consumer Instance 2 ] <--- Consumes P2, P3

SCENARIO 2: 4 Consumer Instances (Optimal: 1 partition each)
  [ Consumer 1 ] <- P0  |  [ Consumer 2 ] <- P1  |  [ Consumer 3 ] <- P2  |  [ Consumer 4 ] <- P3

SCENARIO 3: 5 Consumer Instances (Idle Instance!)
  [ Consumer 5 ] sits 100% IDLE (Partitions cannot be split among consumers in the same group)

sections.heading: Exclusive Partition Ownership and Group Coordination
sections.body: Consumer groups are how Kafka scales consumption horizontally while preserving partition-level ordering. When multiple consumer instances register with the same `group.id`, a broker designated as the Group Coordinator assigns partitions among them. Each partition is assigned to exactly one consumer instance within the group, guaranteeing that concurrent workers never step on each other or process the same partition out of order.
bullets: Concurrency Ceiling: The maximum number of active consumers in a group is strictly bounded by the number of partitions. Extra consumer instances remain idle standbys.

Heartbeat and Session Timeouts: Consumers send background heartbeats to the Group Coordinator (`heartbeat.interval.ms = 3000`). If a consumer misses heartbeats for longer than `session.timeout.ms` (e.g., 45 seconds), the coordinator marks it dead and triggers a rebalance.

codeSnippet.title: Kafka Consumer Configuration with Cooperative Sticky Assignor

sections.heading: Rebalance Storms and Cooperative Sticky Assignment
sections.body: Whenever a consumer joins, crashes, or takes too long to process a batch (`max.poll.interval.ms`), the group triggers a rebalance. In older Kafka versions, rebalances used the Eager Protocol: all consumers stopped processing, revoked all assigned partitions, and waited for the coordinator to reassign the entire cluster. This produced stop-the-world pauses lasting seconds to minutes.
bullets: The Stop-the-World Problem: Under eager rebalancing, a single flapping consumer container causes the entire fleet to repeatedly halt processing, causing consumer lag to skyrocket.

Cooperative Sticky Assignor (Incremental Rebalance): Instead of revoking all partitions, consumers continue processing unaffected partitions uninterrupted. Only the specific partitions migrating from or to the joining/leaving node are paused and reassigned, cutting rebalance pauses from minutes to milliseconds.

tradeOffs.pros: Zero global stop-the-world downtime; unaffected partitions continue processing; minimal latency impact during pod deployments.
tradeOffs.cons: Requires modern Kafka clients (2.4+); rebalance occurs across two incremental rounds.
tradeOffs.bestFor: All modern production Kafka consumer deployments on Kubernetes.

tradeOffs.cons: Freezes all consumers during any node join, restart, or deployment, triggering cascading lag.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Legacy systems unable to upgrade client libraries.

interviewTip: When discussing consumer group scaling, mention the partition ceiling and cooperative rebalancing: 'Consumer concurrency is strictly capped by partition count: you cannot have more active consumers in a group than partitions. To prevent deployment rollouts from halting consumption, we configure the `CooperativeStickyAssignor` so unaffected partitions process continuously while pods restart.'
